questiontext.text: What best describes an Exception in Java?

answer.text: An object that signals an unusual condition during program execution

feedback.text: Correct. Exceptions are objects used to signal runtime problems.

answer.text: A syntax error detected by the compiler

feedback.text: Incorrect. Syntax errors are caught at compile time.

answer.text: A logic error that produces the wrong output

feedback.text: Incorrect. Logic errors do not throw exceptions.
Incorrect. Exceptions are not debugging tools.

questiontext.text: Why did the program crash with an InputMismatchException in the Shop app?

answer.text: The user entered a String when an int was expected

feedback.text: Correct. Scanner.nextInt() cannot read a String.

answer.text: The file could not be found

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would cause a file-related exception.
Incorrect. An empty list does not cause this exception.
Incorrect. That would cause a NullPointerException.

questiontext.text: Which statement about RuntimeExceptions is true?

answer.text: They occur at runtime and can often be avoided with good programming practices

feedback.text: Correct. RuntimeExceptions are not checked by the compiler.

answer.text: They must be caught or declared

feedback.text: Incorrect. That applies to checked exceptions.
Incorrect. Syntax errors stop compilation.

answer.text: They only occur when reading files

feedback.text: Incorrect. RuntimeExceptions can occur anywhere.

questiontext.text: What is the main purpose of a try-catch block?

answer.text: To handle exceptions and allow the program to continue

feedback.text: Correct. try-catch prevents program crashes.
Incorrect. It handles errors after they occur.
Incorrect. try-catch does not improve performance.
Incorrect. try-catch is not a conditional replacement.

questiontext.text: Why was the ScannerInput class introduced?

answer.text: To handle invalid user input using try-catch and prevent crashes

feedback.text: Correct. It validates input and recovers from errors.
Incorrect. It has nothing to do with collections.
Incorrect. That is done using XStream.
Incorrect. Its purpose is robustness, not speed.

questiontext.text: What does persistence mean in programming?

answer.text: Data continues to exist beyond the life of the program

feedback.text: Correct. Persistent data survives program shutdown.
Incorrect. That is volatile storage.
Incorrect. Variables are volatile.

answer.text: Data displayed on a web page

feedback.text: Incorrect. Display is unrelated to persistence.

questiontext.text: What is the main purpose of XML compared to HTML?

answer.text: XML describes and stores data, HTML displays data

feedback.text: Correct. XML focuses on meaning, not presentation.
Incorrect. XML is not a replacement for HTML.

answer.text: XML is used for styling web pages

feedback.text: Incorrect. CSS handles styling.

answer.text: HTML is used to store Java objects

feedback.text: Incorrect. Objects are not stored in HTML.

answer.text: Converting objects into a stream of bytes for storage

feedback.text: Correct. This allows objects to be saved to files.
Incorrect. Serialization is about storage.
Incorrect. Sorting is unrelated.
Incorrect. Input validation uses Scanner and try-catch.

questiontext.text: What is XStream used for in the Shop application?

answer.text: Saving and loading Java objects to and from XML

feedback.text: Correct. XStream handles XML serialization.
Incorrect. ScannerInput handles input.
Incorrect. XStream does not display XML.
Incorrect. XStream works with collections.

questiontext.text: Which action occurs when calling the save() method?

answer.text: Objects are written to an XML file on the hard disk

feedback.text: Correct. save() serializes objects to XML.
Incorrect. save() does not display data.
Incorrect. Objects remain in memory.
Incorrect. save() does not exit the program.

questiontext.text: Why are save() and load() calls placed inside try-catch blocks?

answer.text: They can throw Exceptions that must be handled

feedback.text: Correct. File and serialization errors may occur.
Incorrect. Speed is not the issue.
Incorrect. ArrayLists do not require try-catch.
Incorrect. The menu calls these methods.

questiontext.text: What happens to program data stored only in memory when the program closes?

answer.text: The data is lost because memory is volatile

feedback.text: Correct. RAM does not persist after shutdown.
Incorrect. Data must be explicitly saved.

answer.text: The data is converted to XML

feedback.text: Incorrect. Serialization must be coded.
Incorrect. Memory is not permanent storage.
